result.title: TRACE: Tracking Multimodal Clinical Trajectories for Inpatient Risk Prediction
result.summary: Accurate inpatient risk prediction requires modeling heterogeneous clinical evidence that accumulates irregularly over time. This challenge spans in-hospital mortality, prolonged length of stay, and readmission, each with task-specific observation windows. Existing multimodal approaches combine structured health record data, chest x-rays, and clinical text, but primarily focus on modality fusion or missing-modality compensation, with limited attention to temporal trajectories over an admission. We propose TRACE (TRAjectory modeling of multimodal Clinical Events), a daily-scale framework organizing clinical events into day-level trajectories, separating day-invariant global context from day-specific local events drawn from EHR data, chest x-rays, radiology reports, and discharge summaries. The trajectory is encoded using temporal attention, allowing unavailable modalities to emit no tokens. A phenotype-guided contrastive objective further organizes admissions under heterogeneous disease distributions. Across cohorts from MIMIC-IV, eICU, and MIMIC-III comprising nearly 180,000 total stays, we evaluate TRACE on mortality, length of stay, and readmission prediction. TRACE achieves the highest AUROC across all nine dataset-task settings and the highest ACC in eight, outperforming baselines. Ablation studies validate our attention masks and contrastive learning, while trajectory-level attribution localizes risk-associated hospital days and modalities.

AI.brief_summary: TRACE 将住院期间的多模态临床证据（EHR、胸片、影像报告、出院小结）组织为日级轨迹，用时间注意力编码并区分全局上下文与当日事件，在死亡、住院时长与再入院预测上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「不可用模态不产生 token」的门控设计与轨迹级归因可供核查：前者可能对应 LVR 中的视觉旁路与证据筛选，后者可能启发 latent 状态的贡献分配分析。
